case.summary: Cardholder C13171 disputed a $55.68 online charge (3558054) on card C13171-K2 and, on validation, denied the whole cluster: three near-identical charges within 21 minutes on 19 December, two larger online purchases on 18 December, and the repeated same-amount charges since July. The card is a very high-volume online card (899 txns/180d, 177 devices), which is exactly why individually the amounts scored low - the abuse is hidden inside the noise. Three prior confirmed card-not-present fraud cases exist on this same card, and two episode transactions used rare device profiles (SM-J700M Build/MMB29K, ALE-L23) shared with cards carrying dozens of confirmed CNP fraud cases. The repeated amount is not a legitimate recurring charge: gaps are irregular and the cardholder denies any subscription. Recommend blocking and reissuing the card, opening a case, filing a report given the shared-device linkage, and monitoring the connected cards.

sar.narrative: This report documents suspected card-not-present (CNP) payment card fraud on card C13171-K2, issued to cardholder C13171, involving five unauthorized online transactions totaling $331.10 between 18 and 19 December 2016. On 18 December 2016, two online purchases were posted at 16:52:43 (transaction 3554288, $85.57) and 18:41:53 (transaction 3554683, $78.56). On 19 December 2016, three near-identical charges posted within 21 minutes through three separate online sessions: 21:48:32 (transaction 3557979, $55.60), 21:50:54 (transaction 3557987, $55.69) and 22:08:56 (transaction 3558054, $55.68); all three sessions presented the device string 'unknown | unknown | chrome 66.0 | unknown', one of which was flagged as New. The charge amounts sat at approximately 1.03 times the card's mean transaction value of $54.02 and therefore returned low model scores (0.44, 0.09 and 0.38), allowing the activity to blend into a very high-volume online card profile of 899 transactions and 177 devices over 180 days. Upon customer validation, the cardholder denied authorizing any of the three 19 December charges, the two 18 December purchases, and the repeated same-amount charges recorded since July, stated they hold no subscription or top-up at that amount, and requested that the card be blocked and reissued. Graph review shows the approximately $55.60 amount recurred 13 times with irregular gaps of 17, 12, 0, 9, 10 and 0 days and a looks_monthly value of false, so it does not qualify as a legitimate recurring charge. Card C13171-K2 already carries three confirmed CNP fraud cases for this same cardholder (CC-3566, $88.07 on 15 September 2016; CC-3422, $124.24 on 13 September 2016; and CC-0056, $40.21 on 3 July 2016), each closed with case creation and a card block. Transactions 3554683 and 3550100 originated from two rare device profiles, 'SM-J700M Build/MMB29K | unknown | chrome 66.0 for android | unknown' (24 cards all-time, 14 in the review window) and 'ALE-L23 Build/HuaweiALE-L23 | unknown | chrome 65.0 for android | unknown' (18 cards all-time, 6 in window), which also appear on cards C11509-K2, C04597-K2, C07562-K2 and C06744-K2, each carrying 10 to 20 confirmed CNP fraud cases. The activity is reported as suspicious because the cardholder denies the transactions, the amounts were deliberately kept close to the card's typical spend and split into rapid repeat charges consistent with amount-splitting to evade detection, and the sessions link to rare device profiles shared across multiple cards with established CNP fraud. The bank blocked and reissued card C13171-K2, opened a fraud case, filed this report on the basis of the shared-device linkage, and placed nine connected cards under monitoring: C11923-K2, C05031-K2, C11509-K2, C04597-K2, C07562-K2, C06744-K2, C09657-K2, C06663-K2 and C11597-K2.
